subject: Renewal: Anchored rate-fuse + capacity uplift discussion
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@nebula-tech.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — capacity uplift and pricing constraints

Neha —

Thanks for the run rate breakdown earlier this quarter. We're getting internal alignment for an expanded deployment into additional product teams and need to lock a renewal by the end of November. High level asks from my side:

- Move from our current 2.5M token monthly commit to a 4.5M token commit for calendar 2027 (phased: 2.5M start, 3.5M @ month 4, 4.5M @ month 7).
- Request a 12-month anchored price hold for the base rate per token (US region).
- A short-term bridge credit to offset Q1 ramp costs while usage normalizes (we expect step-ups).

Can Redwood put together 2–3 structured options that balance an anchored rate hold, a commit-bump discount ladder, and some kind of credit or true-up mechanism? Procurement will want specifics (credits, milestone triggers, and any carry-forward rules). Attached is our renewal briefing.

Procurement contact: procurement@nebula-tech.com (cc'd on follow-ups).

Appreciate a quick POV and proposed call slots next week.

—Jordan
Procurement & Partnerships
Nebula Tech
attachments: Nebula_RFP_renewal.pdf

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity uplift and pricing constraints

Jordan —

Thanks for the brief and clear asks. Ben and Monica are looped in — Ben will draft pricing scenarios and Monica will validate operational constraints (burst margin, onboarding runway).

We can definitely do three structured options:
1) Anchored rate-hold + staged commit uplift + small bridge credit tied to Q1 usage milestones.
2) Larger commit-bump with stepped discount tiers (higher upfront commit -> higher discount), limited carry-forward.
3) A hybrid "rate-fuse" option: an anchored base rate with a short-term supplementary tier ("fuse") that absorbs surge consumption at a slightly higher pre-agreed rate; credits apply if surges normalize.

Would you be available for a 30-min alignment on Tuesday 2 Nov 10:00–10:30 PT or Wednesday 3 Nov 14:00–14:30 PT?

I'll ask Ben to circulate a spreadsheet with the line-item scenarios ahead of the call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: RI pricing scenarios for Nebula Tech (attached)

Jordan / Neha / Monica —

Sending the three scenarios as promised (attached): RI_Pricing_Scenarios_Nebula.xlsx. High-level callouts below — numbers are illustrative and assume US region standard model family (mid-range throughput / 8k context):

Option A — Anchored Price Hold + Bridge Credit
- 12-month base rate hold on the current token price for committed usage.
- Commit path: 2.5M -> 3.5M @ month 4 -> 4.5M @ month 7.
- One-time bridge credit = $120k USD applied in Q1 invoices; amortized as a usage credit through Q1–Q2.
- Carry-forward rule: unused committed tokens roll forward for up to 2 months only.

Option B — Commit-Bump Discount Ladder
- Discount increases with commit tranches: 10% at 3M; 16% at 3.5M; 22% at 4.5M (off list rate).
- No bridge credit; lower base list rate.
- True-ups quarterly; unused tokens convert to credits for 3 months.

Option C — Anchored Rate-Fuse (hybrid)
- 12-month anchored base rate for committed usage.
- A temporary "fuse" tier (surge band) for excess consumption during Q1 at a pre-agreed higher rate (about +15% over base).
- If average monthly surge percentage falls below 8% for three consecutive months post-Q1, a reconciliation credit equal to 50% of surge spend is issued.
- Credits capped at $150k; credit vesting tied to usage milestone (50% of uplift committed used by month 6).

Operational notes (Monica):
- We can guarantee dedicated capacity pool for the committed baseline with a 2-week onboarding buffer for additional shard capacity.
- Burst pool availability for the fuse tier is regional — US available, EU would require additional capacity planning.

Next steps: confirm which option to refine and whether procurement needs a rate-hold letter (legal signoff + DocuSign).

Attachments: RI_Pricing_Scenarios_Nebula.xlsx

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@nebula-tech.com>

Cc: procurement@nebula-tech.com, Elena Soto <elena.soto@nebula-tech.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RI pricing scenarios for Nebula Tech (attached)

Ben / Team —

Appreciate the clear scenarios. Internal notes from procurement and engineering: 

- Procurement strongly prefers Option A (anchored rate-hold + bridge credit) for budgeting simplicity, but we need clarity on how credits are amortized and whether any invoice timing exposure exists.
- Engineering likes Option C's fuse concept because it limits long-term commitment for edge teams, but asks that the surge reconciliation logic be automated (we'll need a reporting hook or monthly delta export).

Two asks before the call:
1) Can Redwood provide a one-page rate-hold letter that our legal team can review?
2) Will you confirm the maximum credit cap and the exact reconciliation math for Option C if we choose that?

Also — are there any SLA or latency guarantees tied to committed capacity vs. fuse consumption? If surge consumption is served from a different pool, we need to understand latency variance and routing fallback.

Thanks — looping in Elena from procurement to coordinate legal review.

—Jordan

Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — internal guidance and guardrails

Team —

Quick internal guidance before the joint call:

- I support presenting Option C as the recommended commercial because it preserves upside while giving Nebula the predictability they asked for.
- Constraints: cap credits at $150k (Ben's cap is fine), require a usage milestone (50% of uplift committed used by month 6) for full credit vesting, and limit carry-forward to 2 months.
- Approve a 12-month rate hold on committed baseline, but include language that surge (fuse) routing may be served from a parallel burst pool with documented latency delta (we must disclose potential 10–20ms median added tail latency for certain model families during extreme surge).
- Please pull Legal for a short rate-hold letter and Ops for a monthly reconciliation export (CSV) to be shared with Nebula.

No deep concessions beyond the cap and milestone — we should protect margin and set clear rollback triggers if usage is materially lower than forecast.

—Marissa
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

Subject: Renewal summary and next steps — Anchored Rate-Fuse (mutual option)

Jordan / Elena —

Thanks for the productive discussion earlier today. Per our call, here is the mutually agreed commercial summary for inclusion in the renewal amendment and the next steps to finalize: 

Commercial summary (agreed):
- Model: Option C — Anchored Rate-Fuse (hybrid).
- Commit path: 2.5M tokens (baseline) -> 3.5M at month 4 -> 4.5M at month 7 (calendar 2027).
- Rate hold: 12 months on baseline committed rate for US region.
- Fuse (surge) band: excess consumption during Q1 charged at +15% over base; surge reconciliation credit = 50% of surge spend if average monthly surge < 8% for three consecutive months after Q1. Credit cap = $150k.
- Bridge credit: one-time $100k applied across Q1 invoices (amended from earlier ask).
- Carry-forward: unused committed tokens roll forward up to 2 months.
- SLA/latency: committed baseline served from dedicated pool; fuse may be served from burst pool with expected median tail latency delta of up to 20ms for specific model families. Ops will provide a monthly reconciliation CSV and a Routable Delta report link.

Operational & legal next steps:
1) Redwood Legal to produce a rate-hold letter and an amendment draft (Ben / Marissa to coordinate).
2) I'll send the DocuSign link for the amendment once Legal confirms language.
3) Ops (Monica) to provision the dedicated baseline pool and enable the monthly reconciliation export.
4) Procurement to confirm final signers; Jordan / Elena to share any redline requests within 48 hours of receiving the draft.
